**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR fix the kubectl top **sort-by=cpu** and **sort-by=memory** options.
The sort-by option doesn't sort correctly the pods and nodes.

Two problems ares fixed in the PR :
- Fix the Swap functions to sort nodes and pods
- Use MilliValue() instead of Values() to compare CPU metrics

issue_context.title: `kubectl top --sort-by` is not sorting correctly
issue_context.body:
The --sort-by option to kubectl top was introduced from v1.15.2 and it accepts only 2 params i.e. cpu and memory.

e.g. 
kubectl top po --all-namespaces --sort-by=cpu
kubectl top po --all-namespaces --sort-by=memory

The output is not in a sorted manner.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.15.2
- Cloud provider: GCP/GKE

review_comments: Why we need to go with `MilliValue` here? Are you aware this can overflow thus causing more errors?

Because CPU metrics are always collected with `MilliValue` (instead of MEMORY metrics which are collected with `Value`)

For exemple, for one sample node, `MilliValue` will return _1628_ and `Value` will return _2_. (Value = MilliValue / 1000 round up)

Another exemple show you existing code at the end of _metrics_printer.go_ file : 

```
func printSingleResourceUsage(out io.Writer, resourceType v1.ResourceName, quantity resource.Quantity) {
	switch resourceType {
	case v1.ResourceCPU:
		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%vm", quantity.MilliValue())
	case v1.ResourceMemory:
		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%vMi", quantity.Value()/(1024*1024))
	default:
		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%v", quantity.Value())
	}
}

```
